issues.reason: LocatedIn is containment ONLY — 'in / at / inside / within' — and the head is never a synonym for a near-fit reading, while the instruction set's own tributary note ('a tributary of the larger river' is the ordinary genitive, untouched by the place-in-place rule) puts an of-genitive like 'the water of the Sunken Cove' on PartOf/Possession, so the query binds a relation no faithful statement parse would store.

gaps_confirmed: an ordinal day-of-year date in a non-Gregorian calendar ('day 120 of Year 1'): the Time term (Day <n>) is specified as the calendar day-of-month beside a Month, and nothing covers a bare day-number with no month, which (Day 120) borrows that slot for
new_gaps: a query over a genitive faces an unmergeable storage fork: the part-test decides PartOf vs the opaque Possession statement-side by judgment, Core patterns' dual-storage list does not name that pair, and a query that picks the other branch returns nothing — acute for a mass constituent of a geographic feature ('the water of the cove'), which is neither of PartOf's two stated jobs (component of an object, member of a group) nor a place-in-place
defect_summary: The compliant conjunct is the ordinary genitive of Possessive / genitive NP — (PartOf $wt $sc) if the water counts as a component of the cove, else the opaque (Possession $wt $sc) — in place of (LocatedIn $wt $sc); everything else in the line stands.
notes: Agent for the self-propelled 'a wraith emerged', Source for 'from the water', Past, ReasonFor and the (Member $sc cove) beside (Name $sc "Sunken Cove") (kind word inside the name) are all correct.
